marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: Give the six-figure grid reference for spot height .437 in the southeastern part of the map extract.
key_points: Six-figure grid reference: 672/3 29 4/5
marking_schemes.model_answer: The six-figure grid reference for spot height .437 in the southeastern part of the map extract is 672/3 29 4/5.
common_errors: Most candidates were unable to figure out the third and the sixth figure.
Some candidates had written the sixth number of the northing with the eastings two-digit number and vice versa.
The three digits of the northings were written first, followed by the eastings three digits.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain the concept of a 6-figure grid reference. Draw attention to Eastings and Northings, and provide practice exercises where Eastings are mentioned first, followed by Northings.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: Aman, a local craftsman, wants to sell his product to a large gathering to earn money instantly. Which settlement should he go to?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Malagaon / Pamera (any one)
key_points: Malagaon or Pamera (any one)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Aman should go to Malagaon or Pamera, as these settlements host large gatherings where he can sell his products.
common_errors: Several candidates mentioned the type of settlement (nucleated) instead of the name of the settlement.
Some candidates did not know or understand what a large gathering is.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise the importance of people gathering at a particular place. Provide hints and guide learners to understand the reasons behind gatherings at specific places and times of the year.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: Aman, a local craftsman, wants to sell his product to a large gathering to earn money instantly. Name the month in which he should visit the settlement named by you above.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: March
key_points: March
marking_schemes.model_answer: Aman should visit the settlement in March, when the large gathering takes place.
common_errors: They mentioned the different names of the villages instead of the month as asked in the question.
A very few candidates mentioned the month correctly despite the first part being attempted incorrectly.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage reading the question multiple times to understand what is being asked.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: On which bank of the Sukli nadi is the settlement of Pamera situated?

key_points: Right bank
marking_schemes.model_answer: The settlement of Pamera is situated on the right bank of the Sukli nadi.

Several candidates mentioned direction or northern/southern side instead of the right bank.
Candidates were unable to figure out the bank of Sukhli Nadi with reference to the Pamera settlement.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the basic concept of the flow of a river, emphasising the need to face the direction of the river's flow while interpreting features.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: Identify the settlement pattern seen in the grid square 6732.

key_points: Scattered / dispersed
marking_schemes.model_answer: The settlement pattern seen in the grid square 6732 is scattered or dispersed.
common_errors: A few candidates were confused about the settlement pattern and drainage pattern.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify the concept of topography at the foundational level.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: Roshan, while travelling from Sirori to Tokra, observed that the surface water sources are dry except for the reservoir near Tokra. What according to you may be the reason for the presence of water in the reservoir in 6832 near Tokra settlement?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: There is a presence of embankment / sluice. / dam/ storing water for irrigation./ only storing water/ for growing crops.
key_points: There is a presence of embankment / sluice / dam
Water is stored for irrigation / for growing crops
marking_schemes.model_answer: The presence of water in the reservoir near Tokra is due to the construction of an embankment, sluice, or dam that stores water for irrigation and growing crops.
common_errors: Most of the candidates gave the wrong answer as they wrote due to streams from contours.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Help visualise an artificial or natural reservoir, highlighting the point of embankment through detailed explanation and description. Explain that any embankment or structure which obstructs or stores water is considered an artificial construction.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: Roshan, while travelling from Sirori to Tokra, observed that the surface water sources are dry except for the reservoir near Tokra. marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: What is the direct distance between Gulabganj to Pithapura? Give your answer in kilometre.

accepted_alternatives: Any value between 1.5 km and 3.5 km
common_errors: Most of the candidates gave the wrong answer.

marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Demonstrate how to measure distances using a scale—both direct distances (as the crow flies) and along the actual path.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: Mention the compass direction of Pithapura from Gulabganj.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: Name two man-made features seen in the grid square 6534.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Post office, permanent hut, metalled road, temple, dispensary, lined perennial well./well/Settlement/hut/ road/ National Highway/ Cart track/ Chattri/ Power line/ Unsurveyed poles houses.

marking_schemes.model_answer: Two man-made features seen in grid square 6534 include a post office and a metalled road (any two valid man-made features from the area are acceptable).
common_errors: A few candidates gave man-made features which were not present in the specified area.
Many responses included hospitals, houses, and a police station, even though they were not present.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Bring clarity about man-made (cultural) and natural features. Correlate their identification with the conventional symbols provided at the end of the map extract.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10 and answer the following questions: Define contour interval.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is the difference in value between two successive/consecutive contour lines. Vertical distance/gap between two successive contours/Difference in height between two successive contour.
key_points: The difference in value between two successive/consecutive contour lines
Vertical distance/gap between two successive contours
marking_schemes.model_answer: Contour interval is the difference in value between two successive or consecutive contour lines, i.e., the vertical distance or gap between two successive contours.
accepted_alternatives: Difference in value between two successive/consecutive contour lines
Vertical distance/gap between two successive contours
Difference in height between two successive contour
common_errors: A large number of candidates confused 'definition of Contour Interval' with 'Vertical interval'.
Many responses mentioned 'the contour interval is 20 m' instead of defining it.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the geographical definitions of contour, contour interval, and vertical interval in class.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Severe cyclonic storms are often formed over the Bay of Bengal during the retreating monsoon season. The temperate cyclones cause less damage than the tropical cyclones. Give any two points to support this statement.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Temperate cyclone winds move with less speed/less stormy/no storms. Temperate Cyclone large area/ beneficial for Rabi Crop. Temperate cyclone brings in light rainfall /drizzle. Gentle pressure Gradient. Whereas tropical cyclonic winds move fast /and bring heavy rainfall which leads to a lot of destruction./ Steep pressure gradient affects small area. (any two)
key_points: Temperate cyclone winds move with less speed/less stormy/no storms
Temperate cyclone covers large area / beneficial for Rabi Crop
Temperate cyclone brings light rainfall/drizzle
Gentle pressure gradient (as opposed to steep pressure gradient of tropical cyclones)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Temperate cyclones cause less damage than tropical cyclones because they move with less speed and bring light rainfall or drizzle, whereas tropical cyclones have steep pressure gradients and bring heavy rainfall causing destruction.
accepted_alternatives: Temperate cyclone winds move with less speed/less stormy/no storms
Temperate Cyclone large area/ beneficial for Rabi Crop
Temperate cyclone brings in light rainfall /drizzle
common_errors: A large number of candidates were not able to apply their knowledge of temperate and tropical cyclones from their previous classes.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Build students' conceptual clarity between the two types of cyclones: tropical cyclones and temperate cyclones.

Lowers the temperature and brings relief

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to Figure A and Figure B given below (Figure A shows winds blowing from sea to land over India, Figure B shows winds blowing from land to sea), name the winds shown by arrows in Figure A and Figure B.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Figure A shows South West monsoon wind / onshore winds/ summer monsoon/approaching monsoon./ advancing monsoon/ sea to land./ Arabian Sea branch/ Bay of Bengal branch. Figure B shows North East monsoon wind /off shore winds/ winter monsoon/retreating monsoon./ Land to sea.
key_points: Figure A: South West monsoon wind / onshore winds / summer monsoon / approaching monsoon / advancing monsoon / sea to land / Arabian Sea branch / Bay of Bengal branch
Figure B: North East monsoon wind / offshore winds / winter monsoon / retreating monsoon / land to sea
marking_schemes.model_answer: Figure A shows the South West monsoon (onshore/summer monsoon blowing from sea to land), while Figure B shows the North East monsoon (offshore/winter monsoon blowing from land to sea).
common_errors: Most of the candidates recognised the winds.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Build clarity on the direction of winds during different monsoon seasons.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to Figure A (winds blowing from sea to land) and Figure B (winds blowing from land to sea), how is the wind shown in Figure A different from the one shown in Figure B?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Wind seen in Figure A is onshore and the one in Figure B is offshore wind. A-Summer Monsoon, B- Retreating Monsoon. Wind seen in Figure A bring rain to most of India and the one in Figure B bring rain to S E coastal areas/ Coromandal Coast/ TN Coast. Wind seen in Figure A blows during summer and the one seen in Figure B blows during winter./ Retreating. Mention of Month/ Any month between- June to September, and October to February.
key_points: Figure A wind is onshore; Figure B wind is offshore
Figure A is Summer Monsoon; Figure B is Retreating/Winter Monsoon
Figure A brings rain to most of India; Figure B brings rain to SE coastal areas/Coromandal Coast/TN Coast
Figure A blows during summer (June to September); Figure B blows during winter (October to February)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The wind in Figure A is an onshore summer monsoon that blows from sea to land during June to September, bringing rain to most parts of India. The wind in Figure B is an offshore retreating/winter monsoon that blows from land to sea during October to February, bringing rain only to the SE coastal areas/Coromandal Coast/Tamil Nadu coast.
common_errors: A large number of candidates were not able to apply their knowledge.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the differences in the duration and period of various types of monsoons.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the climate data of station X (Jan: 24.0°C/0.25cm, Feb: 25.4°C/0.25cm, Mar: 26.7°C/-, Apr: 28.3°C/-, May: 30.0°C/1.75cm, June: 28.9°C/50.2cm, July: 27.6°C/61.0cm, Aug: 27.4°C/37.0cm, Sep: 27.3°C/27.0cm, Oct: 27.1°C/4.75cm, Nov: 27.0°C/1.50cm, Dec: 25.0°C/-) and answer: What is the annual range of temperature for station X?
marking_schemes.model_answer: The annual range of temperature for station X is 6°C (30.0°C - 24.0°C).
common_errors: In some instances, the candidates were not able to mention the 'units'.
Calculation errors were found.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise the importance of mentioning units in calculation-based questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the climate data of station X (Jan: 24.0°C/0.25cm, Feb: 25.4°C/0.25cm, Mar: 26.7°C/-, Apr: 28.3°C/-, May: 30.0°C/1.75cm, June: 28.9°C/50.2cm, July: 27.6°C/61.0cm, Aug: 27.4°C/37.0cm, Sep: 27.3°C/27.0cm, Oct: 27.1°C/4.75cm, Nov: 27.0°C/1.50cm, Dec: 25.0°C/-) and answer: Which is the wettest month?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: July is the wettest month.
key_points: July is the wettest month
marking_schemes.model_answer: July is the wettest month for station X, with a rainfall of 61.0 cm.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to carefully read and interpret data before answering questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the climate data of station X (Jan: 24.0°C/0.25cm, Feb: 25.4°C/0.25cm, Mar: 26.7°C/-, Apr: 28.3°C/-, May: 30.0°C/1.75cm, June: 28.9°C/50.2cm, July: 27.6°C/61.0cm, Aug: 27.4°C/37.0cm, Sep: 27.3°C/27.0cm, Oct: 27.1°C/4.75cm, Nov: 27.0°C/1.50cm, Dec: 25.0°C/-) and answer: Name the wind which brings rainfall for station X during the rainy season.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: South west monsoon wind./ Summer monsoon/advancing monsoon. / Approaching Monsoon.
key_points: South west monsoon wind / Summer monsoon / Advancing monsoon / Approaching monsoon
marking_schemes.model_answer: The South West monsoon wind (summer monsoon/advancing monsoon) brings rainfall for station X during the rainy season.
common_errors: Only a few candidates mentioned it as 'Retreating Monsoon'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explore local winds in depth, along with broader atmospheric circulation patterns.

marking_schemes.question_text: The Ganga Plain is known for its fertile soil. It is often referred to as the food bowl of India. This region supports a variety of crops such as rice, wheat, pulses, jute and sugarcane. Name the soil that is found in large parts of Ganga plain.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Alluvial soil / Khadar/bangar/new alluvium/old alluvium./ in land alluvium.
key_points: Alluvial soil / Khadar / Bangar / New alluvium / Old alluvium / Inland alluvium
marking_schemes.model_answer: The soil found in large parts of the Ganga plain is alluvial soil (also known as Khadar, Bangar, new alluvium, or old alluvium).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the formation and distribution of each type of soil using maps.

marking_schemes.question_text: The Ganga Plain is known for its fertile soil. It is often referred to as the food bowl of India. This region supports a variety of crops such as rice, wheat, pulses, jute and sugarcane. Give two properties of this soil which helps it to produce a variety of crops.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Alluvial soil is rich in Potash, lime, humus, iron, magnesium, calcium, aluminium (can be taken as separate points) / it is renewed or replenished or fresh deposition / friable or easily cultivable/moisture retentive/fine textured/responds to fertilizers/loamy./ It is fertile/ deep. (any two)
key_points: Rich in nutrients: Potash, lime, humus, iron, magnesium, calcium, aluminium
Renewed/replenished/fresh deposition
Friable/easily cultivable
Moisture retentive
Fine textured
Responds to fertilizers
Loamy/fertile/deep
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two properties of alluvial soil that help produce a variety of crops are that it is rich in nutrients like potash, lime, and humus, and it is moisture retentive and fine textured, making it easily cultivable.
common_errors: A few candidates mentioned that it contains clay to hold moisture.
Candidates found it difficult to grasp the characteristics of various soil types, such as texture, porosity, and colour.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the properties and composition of different soils as per the syllabus.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is meant by soil erosion?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is the removal and / or destruction of top soil due to running water, wind or activities of man./ it is removal of fertile soil/removal of top layer of soil/depletion of top soil/ degradation/ detachment and removal/ detachment and transportation.
key_points: Removal and/or destruction of top soil due to running water, wind, or activities of man
Removal of fertile soil/top layer of soil/depletion of top soil/degradation/detachment and removal/detachment and transportation
marking_schemes.model_answer: Soil erosion is the removal and/or destruction of the top soil due to running water, wind, or activities of man, leading to depletion or degradation of the fertile soil layer.
accepted_alternatives: Removal and/or destruction of top soil due to running water, wind or activities of man
Removal of top layer of soil
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain soil erosion, its causes by different agents, and the importance of soil conservation methods.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name any two agents of soil erosion.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Running water, wind./ man/ sea waves/ water. (any two)
key_points: Any two from: Running water, wind, man, sea waves, water
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two agents of soil erosion are running water and wind.
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned Anthropogenic factors as agents of soil erosion.
A few candidates mentioned causes in place of agents.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain soil erosion, its causes by different agents, and the importance of soil conservation methods.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason to explain each of the following: Soil conservation is the need of the hour.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is needed to preserve and protect the fertile layer so that the productivity of soil is retained./ to preserve soil for feeding growing population/if soil is not conserved it may lead to scarcity of food./ Soil takes a long time to form so it should be consumed.
key_points: Needed to preserve and protect the fertile layer so that productivity of soil is retained
To preserve soil for feeding growing population / if soil is not conserved it may lead to scarcity of food
Soil takes a long time to form so it should be conserved
marking_schemes.model_answer: Soil conservation is the need of the hour because it is needed to preserve and protect the fertile layer so that the productivity of soil is retained and to feed the growing population; if soil is not conserved it may lead to scarcity of food.
accepted_alternatives: To preserve and protect the fertile layer so that productivity is retained
To preserve soil for feeding growing population
If soil is not conserved it may lead to scarcity of food
Soil takes a long time to form so it should be conserved
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain soil erosion, its causes by different agents, and the importance of soil conservation methods.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason to explain each of the following: Red soil has a poor water retention capacity.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Red soil is porous./coarse texture./ loose soil.
key_points: Red soil is porous / coarse texture / loose soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: Red soil has a poor water retention capacity because it is porous, has a coarse texture, and is loose in nature, which allows water to drain quickly.
common_errors: Several candidates mentioned that Red Soil contains a high amount of iron oxide; hence, it has low moisture retention capacity.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Build clarity on the characteristics of specific soils, such as Laterite soil.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason to explain each of the following: Laterite soils are infertile.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is due to leaching/ poor in nitrogen, lime, phosphorus, magnesium, organic matter/poor water retention/acidic/poor in silica/poor in nutrients.
key_points: Due to leaching
Poor in nitrogen, lime, phosphorus, magnesium, organic matter
Poor water retention / acidic / poor in silica / poor in nutrients
marking_schemes.model_answer: Laterite soils are infertile because they are subjected to heavy leaching which removes nutrients, making them poor in nitrogen, lime, phosphorus, magnesium, and organic matter, and they are also acidic in nature.
accepted_alternatives: Poor in nitrogen, lime, phosphorus, magnesium, organic matter
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Build clarity on the characteristics of specific soils, such as Laterite soil.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to black soil of India, answer the following questions: How is this soil formed?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is formed by weathering of lava rocks./disintegration of volcanic/basaltic/extrusive igneous rocks/ Basic igneous solidification of basic lava.
key_points: Formed by weathering of lava rocks / disintegration of volcanic/basaltic/extrusive igneous rocks / Basic igneous solidification of basic lava
marking_schemes.model_answer: Black soil is formed by the weathering and disintegration of volcanic/basaltic/extrusive igneous rocks or the solidification of basic lava.
accepted_alternatives: Basic igneous solidification of basic lava
common_errors: In some cases, candidates mentioned that Black Soil is formed by the denudation of lava rocks.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the formation and distribution of each type of soil using maps.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to black soil of India, answer the following questions: How is this soil able to retain moisture for a long period?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It has clayey nature./fine textured/sticky when wet
key_points: Clayey nature / fine textured / sticky when wet
marking_schemes.model_answer: Black soil is able to retain moisture for a long period because it has a clayey nature, is fine textured, and becomes sticky when wet, which prevents water from draining away quickly.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the properties and composition of different soils as per the syllabus.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to black soil of India, answer the following questions: Mention any two minerals present in this soil.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Lime, iron, magnesium, calcium, alumina, potash (LIMCAP) (any two)
key_points: Any two from: Lime, iron, magnesium, calcium, alumina, potash
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two minerals present in black soil are lime and iron (any two from: lime, iron, magnesium, calcium, alumina, potash).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the properties and composition of different soils as per the syllabus.

marking_schemes.question_text: India has lost 2.33 million hectares of tree cover since the year 2000. This is equivalent to a six percent decrease in tree cover during this period. Mention any two causes of the decrease in the forest cover of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Deforestation, urbanisation, industrialisation, overgrazing, land for agriculture/ modernisation/demand for timber or furniture/forest fire./ Construction of multipurpose project/ dam/ construction/ Population pressure/ Mining/ Quarrying/ Shifting agriculture. (any two)
key_points: Any two from: Deforestation, urbanisation, industrialisation, overgrazing, land for agriculture, modernisation, demand for timber or furniture, forest fire, construction of multipurpose project/dam, population pressure, mining, quarrying, shifting agriculture
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two causes of the decrease in forest cover of India are deforestation for agriculture and urbanisation/industrialisation.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Build clarity of concept on the reasons for decrease of forest cover in India.

marking_schemes.question_text: India has lost 2.33 million hectares of tree cover since the year 2000. Name a conservation method that may be used to help in increasing the forest cover.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Afforestation, Agro forestry, social forestry, Van Mahotsav/reafforestation/controlled grazing/creating fire line/silviculture/farm forestry/ Chipko/ Planting trees in different areas. (any one)
key_points: Any one from: Afforestation, Agro forestry, Social forestry, Van Mahotsav, Reafforestation, Controlled grazing, Creating fire line, Silviculture, Farm forestry, Chipko, Planting trees in different areas
marking_schemes.model_answer: A conservation method that may be used to help increase the forest cover is afforestation or social forestry.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to learn different methods of conservation of forests in India.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention the climatic condition suitable for the development of tropical evergreen forest.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Tropical evergreen forest: 20-30 degree Celsius; 150-350 cm rainfall/over 200 cms; 70-95% humidity (Any one point)
key_points: Temperature: 20-30 degree Celsius
Rainfall: 150-350 cm / over 200 cm
Humidity: 70-95%
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical evergreen forests develop in conditions of high temperature (20-30°C), very heavy rainfall (150-350 cm or over 200 cm), and high humidity (70-95%).
common_errors: Some candidates were confused about temperature and rainfall and provided incorrect answers.
They were unable to comprehend the specific types and features of forests, as well as the connection between vegetation and climate.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Illustrate in class the various climatic conditions that are linked to vegetation types, using images of different forests and vegetation found in diverse climates.

marking_schemes.question_text: State any three differences between tropical deciduous and tropical desert vegetation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Tropical deciduous: Pure stand, easy to exploit, hard durable wood/denser/economic value/shed their leaves/broad leaves/tall trees/names of trees to be accepted. Humidity- 50 to 70%. Rain-100-200 cm. Temperature-20-30°C. Tropical Desert: Stunted trees, long roots, waxy leaves, spines, fleshy stem, scattered growth/names of trees to be accepted/xerophytes. Humidity-Less than 50%. Rain-Less than 50 cm. Temperature-20-35°C. (any three)
key_points: Tropical deciduous: Pure stand, hard durable wood, shed their leaves, broad leaves, tall trees; Tropical desert: Stunted trees, long roots, waxy leaves, spines, fleshy stem, scattered growth/xerophytes
Tropical deciduous: Humidity 50-70%; Tropical desert: Humidity less than 50%
Tropical deciduous: Rain 100-200 cm; Tropical desert: Rain less than 50 cm
Tropical deciduous: Temperature 20-30°C; Tropical desert: Temperature 20-35°C
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical deciduous forests have tall trees with broad leaves that shed during dry season, humidity of 50-70%, and rainfall of 100-200 cm, whereas tropical desert vegetation consists of stunted xerophytes with waxy leaves, spines, and fleshy stems, with humidity less than 50% and rainfall less than 50 cm.
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'tropical evergreen vegetation' instead of 'tropical desert'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Revise the characteristics of each natural vegetation belt.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give any two reasons for the great diversity of natural vegetation in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Variety of soil, diverse climatic condition, physiography/relief/vast size of the country./ Latitude Extent is vast. (any two)
key_points: Variety of soil
Diverse climatic condition
Physiography/relief/vast size of the country/Vast latitude extent
marking_schemes.model_answer: The great diversity of natural vegetation in India is due to the variety of soils and diverse climatic conditions across the country, along with the vast size and varying physiography/relief.
common_errors: Majority of the candidates wrote 'the importance of trees' or 'the importance of forests' instead of 'reasons for the great diversity of natural vegetation'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to learn the reasons for the great diversity of natural vegetation in India.

marking_schemes.question_text: How do the forests help in maintenance of air quality?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Forest give out oxygen / absorb carbon dioxide / Purifies the air./ Carbon sink./ Forest help in bringing rain which in turns improves air quality and control air pollution.
key_points: Forests give out oxygen / absorb carbon dioxide / purify the air / act as carbon sink
Forests help in bringing rain which improves air quality and controls air pollution
marking_schemes.model_answer: Forests help in maintenance of air quality by giving out oxygen, absorbing carbon dioxide, and acting as carbon sinks. They also help in bringing rain, which in turn improves air quality and controls air pollution.
accepted_alternatives: Help in bringing rain which improves air quality and controls air pollution
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain to students the role of the forests in human lives.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention any one advantage and any one disadvantage of well irrigation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Advantage: Cheap, easy to operate, usage in hand of farmer, can be dug at convenient place, independent source./occupy small area./ Easy to dig. (any one) Disadvantage: Dries up, manual labour, irrigate small fields/pollution./ Water pollution./ time consuming (any one)
key_points: Advantage: any one from: cheap, easy to operate, usage in hand of farmer, can be dug at convenient place, independent source, occupy small area, easy to dig
Disadvantage: any one from: dries up, manual labour, irrigate small fields, pollution, water pollution, time consuming
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of well irrigation is that it is cheap and easy to operate, with usage under the control of the farmer. One disadvantage is that wells can dry up during summer and can only irrigate small fields.
accepted_alternatives: Can be dug at convenient place
common_errors: A few of the candidates mentioned that it cannot be constructed in hilly regions.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss elaborately in class, 'merits and demerits of Well irrigation'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Suggest any two measures to overcome scarcity of water in the metropolitan cities of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Rainwater harvesting, recharging ground water, installing water metres, spreading awareness through social media, dug well, bore well, permeable pavement, percolation pit./revival of ancient methods/reuse of water./ watershed management./ Waste water treatment./ Recycling of waste water. (any two)
key_points: Any two from: Rainwater harvesting, recharging ground water, installing water metres, spreading awareness through social media, dug well, bore well, permeable pavement, percolation pit, revival of ancient methods, reuse of water, watershed management, waste water treatment, recycling of waste water
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two measures to overcome water scarcity in metropolitan cities are rainwater harvesting and recharging ground water through percolation pits or bore wells.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the water crisis faced by India and remedies to overcome it.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: Tank irrigation is NOT common in Northern India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Soft soil, large number of rivers/absence of natural depressions/other better sources are easily available./ Absence of hand rock.
key_points: Soft soil / large number of rivers / absence of natural depressions / other better sources are easily available / absence of hard rock
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tank irrigation is not common in Northern India because the soil is soft (not hard rock) and there are large number of rivers and absence of natural depressions; other better sources of irrigation are easily available.
accepted_alternatives: Other better sources are easily available
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students about the type of terrain necessary for the development of various means of irrigation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: Canal irrigation is important in Punjab.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Perennial rivers, soft soil, agriculture is important/fertile agricultural land to recover the cost/level land or flat plain
key_points: Perennial rivers / soft soil / agriculture is important / fertile agricultural land to recover the cost / level land or flat plain
marking_schemes.model_answer: Canal irrigation is important in Punjab because it has perennial rivers, soft and level land, and agriculture is economically important; the fertile agricultural land helps recover the cost of canal construction.
accepted_alternatives: Fertile agricultural land to recover the cost
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss and explain the uses of canal irrigation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: All farmers do not use tube well irrigation even if the geographical condition is favourable.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is expensive / need cheap electricity/lack of power supply/depletes groundwater (any one)
key_points: Expensive / needs cheap electricity / lack of power supply / depletes groundwater
marking_schemes.model_answer: All farmers do not use tube well irrigation even if geographical conditions are favourable because it is expensive to install and requires a reliable and cheap electricity supply, which may not be available in all areas.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Show a comparative study of different means of irrigation with the advantages and disadvantages of each type.

marking_schemes.question_text: State any three objectives of rainwater harvesting.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Will help in water conservation. Recharging ground water. Reduces water scarcity. Clean water availability. Checks soil erosion. Reduce flooding/ Reduce surface runoff. Meets the increasing demand for water. Checks groundwater pollution. Supplement water supply during dry period/ Summer. (any three)
key_points: Will help in water conservation
Recharging ground water
Reduces water scarcity
Clean water availability
Checks soil erosion
Reduce flooding / reduce surface runoff
Meets the increasing demand for water
Checks groundwater pollution
Supplement water supply during dry period/summer
marking_schemes.model_answer: Three objectives of rainwater harvesting are: (1) to help in water conservation and recharging ground water, (2) to reduce water scarcity and meet the increasing demand for water, and (3) to check soil erosion and reduce flooding by reducing surface runoff.
accepted_alternatives: Meets the increasing demand for water
Supplement water supply during dry period/summer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Describe the concept of rainwater harvesting with its importance.

marking_schemes.question_text: With the rising price of fossil fuel every passing day, it is very important to develop non-conventional energy resource. Name a non-conventional energy source that can be harnessed by taking advantage of India's vast coastline.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Tidal energy/wind energy
key_points: Tidal energy / wind energy
marking_schemes.model_answer: A non-conventional energy source that can be harnessed by taking advantage of India's vast coastline is tidal energy or wind energy.
common_errors: Majority of the candidates did not pay attention to the question and mentioned solar energy/wind energy, as they skipped to read the word 'vast coastline'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain how relief structures are responsible for deciding the type of non-conventional energy.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one advantage of using geothermal energy.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Eco friendly / renewable / inexhaustible/sustainable (any one)
key_points: Eco friendly / renewable / inexhaustible / sustainable
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of using geothermal energy is that it is eco-friendly, renewable, and inexhaustible.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in class the advantages of non-conventional energy.

marking_schemes.question_text: How is Biogas formed?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is the gas obtained by decomposition of vegetative and animal waste.
key_points: Gas obtained by decomposition of vegetative and animal waste
marking_schemes.model_answer: Biogas is formed by the decomposition of vegetative and animal waste in the absence of oxygen.
common_errors: Some candidates were not able to explain the process of biogas formation.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept and procedure of biogas formation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention any one advantage of Biogas over other non-conventional energy resources.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Raw material is easily available, cheap, waste is reduced, extra income./waste of farm is recycled/sludge is used as manure./ Keeps the village clean. (any one)
key_points: Raw material is easily available / cheap / waste is reduced / extra income / waste of farm is recycled / sludge is used as manure / keeps the village clean
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of biogas over other non-conventional energy resources is that raw material (vegetative and animal waste) is easily available and cheap, and the leftover sludge can be used as manure.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to build conceptual clarity so that they can differentiate between other non-conventional energy resources.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: Iron ore is called a versatile mineral.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is used for making steel which in turn is used for varied purpose – from needle to space craft is made with its help./any use of iron
key_points: Used for making steel which is used for varied purposes – from needle to spacecraft / any use of iron
marking_schemes.model_answer: Iron ore is called a versatile mineral because it is used for making steel, which in turn is used for a wide variety of purposes, from making a needle to constructing a spacecraft.
accepted_alternatives: Used for making steel which is used for varied purposes
From needle to space craft is made with its help
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to mention the uses of minerals.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: Windmills set up on agricultural lands are beneficial to farmers.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Added income / source of cheap power that is renewable./power may be used for tube well irrigation or for running motor pumps.
key_points: Added income / source of cheap renewable power / power may be used for tube well irrigation or for running motor pumps
marking_schemes.model_answer: Windmills set up on agricultural lands are beneficial to farmers because they provide added income and a source of cheap renewable power, which may be used for tube well irrigation or for running motor pumps.
accepted_alternatives: Source of cheap power that is renewable
Power may be used for tube well irrigation or for running motor pumps
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give explanations regarding the benefits of multipurpose dams.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: Coal is the most preferred source of energy in Indian industries.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: High calorific value, easily available. (any one)
key_points: High calorific value / easily available
marking_schemes.model_answer: Coal is the most preferred source of energy in Indian industries because it has a high calorific value and is easily available.
common_errors: A few of the candidates mentioned 'the use of coal' instead of 'the energy source that was most preferred'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the advantages of conventional energy resources.

marking_schemes.question_text: A picture shows a concrete dam with reservoir, spillway gates, and erosion protection. Identify the type of energy being generated in the picture given above.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Hydel power
key_points: Hydel power
marking_schemes.model_answer: The type of energy being generated in the picture is hydel power (hydroelectric power).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the advantages of hydel energy.

marking_schemes.question_text: A picture shows a concrete dam with reservoir, spillway gates, and erosion protection. State why this type of energy (hydel power) is cheaper in the long run.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Less maintenance cost and no expenditure needed for raw material/ low recurring cost/abundantly available/cheaply available./ Renewable/inexhaustible.
key_points: Less maintenance cost and no expenditure needed for raw material / low recurring cost / abundantly available / cheaply available / renewable / inexhaustible
marking_schemes.model_answer: Hydel power is cheaper in the long run because it has less maintenance cost, no expenditure is needed for raw material (water), and it is renewable and inexhaustible.
accepted_alternatives: Less maintenance cost and no expenditure needed for raw material
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the advantages of hydel energy.

marking_schemes.question_text: A picture shows a concrete dam with reservoir, spillway gates, and erosion protection. Name a power project associated with the generation of this energy (hydel power) in the northern part of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bhakra Nangal
key_points: Bhakra Nangal
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Bhakra Nangal power project is associated with the generation of hydel power in the northern part of India.
common_errors: A few did not pay attention to the part of the question that asked 'which northern part of India' and thus lost marks.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Build awareness of students towards the names of states benefited by the projects.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two climatic conditions that favour the cultivation of groundnut.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Temperature: 20º – 30ºC Cannot withstand frost Around 25/ About 25. Rainfall: 50 - 100 cm Around 70/ About 70 (any two)
key_points: Temperature: 20°C - 30°C / cannot withstand frost / around 25°C
Rainfall: 50-100 cm / around 70 cm
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two climatic conditions that favour the cultivation of groundnut are a temperature range of 20°C to 30°C (cannot withstand frost) and a rainfall of 50-100 cm.
common_errors: Several candidates mentioned the range of temperature and rainfall incorrectly.
Some candidates mentioned only one value instead of the range.
Other candidates wrote vague points like hot climate, dry climate.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to prepare a table for crops, their areas, climatic and soil requirements.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give any two reasons why Maharashtra has emerged as an important sugarcane producing state.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Black soil. Tropical climate / maritime climate. Temperature: 20 – 30°C. Rain: 100 – 200 cm. Frost free days. Scientifically managed / cooperative farming / capital investment from sugar lobby / Sugar industry located close to plantation./ Absence of loo. (any two)
key_points: Black soil
Tropical/maritime climate
Temperature: 20-30°C
Rain: 100-200 cm
Frost free days
Scientifically managed / cooperative farming / capital investment from sugar lobby / sugar industry located close to plantation / absence of loo
marking_schemes.model_answer: Maharashtra has emerged as an important sugarcane producing state because of its black soil and tropical/maritime climate with temperatures of 20-30°C, adequate rainfall of 100-200 cm, frost-free days, and scientifically managed cooperative farming with capital investment from the sugar lobby.
accepted_alternatives: Sugar industry located close to plantation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Use a map while teaching, so that students get a clearer idea about the benefits of Maharashtra being beside the sea for growing sugarcane.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: Trees are planted in between the rows of coffee plants.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: To provide shade / extra income
key_points: To provide shade / extra income
marking_schemes.model_answer: Trees are planted in between the rows of coffee plants to provide shade to the coffee plants and to generate extra income.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to understand and learn instead of rote learning.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: Cotton cultivation requires plenty of cheap labour.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: For picking, ginning, manuring. Harvesting
key_points: For picking, ginning, manuring, harvesting
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cotton cultivation requires plenty of cheap labour because the processes of picking, ginning, manuring, and harvesting cannot be done entirely by machinery and require intensive manual labour.
common_errors: A large number of candidates were not able to answer this; they either left it or wrote in general about cotton cultivation.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Mention the reason crops like jute, cotton need lot of labour as work cannot be done by machinery.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: Hill slopes are best suited for tea cultivation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Stagnant water is harmful for crop./require well drained soil
key_points: Stagnant water is harmful for the crop / requires well drained soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: Hill slopes are best suited for tea cultivation because stagnant water is harmful for the crop and hill slopes provide the well-drained soil necessary for tea bushes to thrive.
accepted_alternatives: Stagnant water is harmful for crop
common_errors: Several candidates wrote about cool climate on hilltops being a factor, or that tea leaves were given a unique flavour by the damp cool weather.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise that the main reason for growing tea bushes on hill slopes is the fact that tea bushes cannot grow in flat land due to stagnant water.

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain the following: Mixed farming
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Growing crops along with rearing of livestock.
key_points: Growing crops along with rearing of livestock
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mixed farming is the practice of growing crops along with rearing of livestock on the same farm.
common_errors: A large number of candidates wrote mixed farming being a mixture of different crops, or cash and food crops.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise the importance of mixed farming being an advantage to farmers. Explain its differences with double or multiple cropping and also from silviculture.

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain the following: Zayad
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Intermediatory/ cropping season between Rabi and Kharif.
key_points: Intermediary/cropping season between Rabi and Kharif
marking_schemes.model_answer: Zayad is the intermediary cropping season between Rabi and Kharif seasons.
accepted_alternatives: Cropping season between Rabi and Kharif
common_errors: A few candidates confused it with Kharif crop.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the three cropping seasons of India, the crops grown and months covered in tabular form.

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain the following: Transplantation
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Growing of rice in nursery and then transplanting the sapling in the main field. Growing of crop in nursery and then transplanting the sapling in the main field
key_points: Growing of rice/crop in nursery and then transplanting the sapling in the main field
marking_schemes.model_answer: Transplantation is the process of growing rice (or other crops) in a nursery first and then transplanting the saplings into the main field.
accepted_alternatives: Growing of rice in nursery and then transplanting the sapling in the main field
Growing of crop in nursery and then transplanting the sapling in the main field
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the topic of transportation with examples and show actual pictures of transplantation.

marking_schemes.question_text: State any two factors that are responsible for the growth of the cotton textile industry in Kolkata.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Humid climate, port facility, transport network, wide market, cheap labour, power supply, coal from Raniganj or Jharia, soft water from Hooghly./ Capital available./ Skilled Labour. (any two)
key_points: Any two from: Humid climate, port facility, transport network, wide market, cheap labour, power supply, coal from Raniganj or Jharia, soft water from Hooghly, capital available, skilled labour
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two factors responsible for the growth of the cotton textile industry in Kolkata are its humid climate and access to port facilities, along with a wide market and cheap labour.
common_errors: Several candidates mentioned advantages like black soil, raw material availability, etc., as they seemed to relate cotton textile industry with the cultivation of cotton in India.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Mention the difference between the two i.e. agriculture and agro-based industries by using a political map while explaining the chapter.

marking_schemes.question_text: 'Karnataka is the leading state for silk production in India.' Give any two reasons to justify the above statement.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Suitable climate for sericulture / mulberry trees. Wide market. Silk worms reared all through the year. Fresh water available/soft water or alkaline free water. Modern scientific technology. Skilled labour available. Bombyxmori is reared throughout the year. Licenced nurseries. Traditional skill. Sericulture provide employment to women. Government Subsidy. (any two)
key_points: Any two from: Suitable climate for sericulture/mulberry trees, wide market, silk worms reared all through the year, fresh water/soft water available, modern scientific technology, skilled labour available, Bombyxmori reared throughout the year, licenced nurseries, traditional skill, sericulture provides employment to women, government subsidy
marking_schemes.model_answer: Karnataka is the leading state for silk production because it has suitable climate for sericulture and mulberry trees, silk worms are reared all through the year, and it has skilled labour with traditional expertise.
accepted_alternatives: Silk worms reared all through the year
Fresh water available/soft water or alkaline free water
Bombyxmori is reared throughout the year
common_errors: Only mistake identified was in the spelling of 'Bombyxmori'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach agriculture and agro-based industries, simultaneously.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the Iron and Steel industry located at Chhattisgarh.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bhillai steel plant
key_points: Bhillai steel plant
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Iron and Steel industry located at Chhattisgarh is the Bhilai Steel Plant.
common_errors: Most of the candidates identified the industry as a different one.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Use a map while teaching, pinpoint the locations of the iron and steel factories.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the Iron and Steel industry located at Chhattisgarh. From where does the industry named by you above (Bhilai Steel Plant) get its supply of Iron ore?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Iron ore – Dalli Rajhara, Bastar/ Durg
key_points: Iron ore from Dalli Rajhara / Bastar / Durg
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Bhilai Steel Plant gets its supply of iron ore from Dalli Rajhara, Bastar, or Durg.
common_errors: Since the industry identified was wrong, the suppliers were also wrongly identified.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Insist that students frequently refer to the maps while learning the chapter to remember the locations.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the Iron and Steel industry located at Chhattisgarh. From where does the industry named by you above (Bhilai Steel Plant) get its supply of Coal?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Coal – Korba, Raniganj, Jharia, Kargati, Bokaro
key_points: Coal from Korba / Raniganj / Jharia / Kargati / Bokaro
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Bhilai Steel Plant gets its supply of coal from Korba, Raniganj, Jharia, Kargati, or Bokaro.
common_errors: Since the industry identified was wrong, the suppliers were also wrongly identified.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Insist that students frequently refer to the maps while learning the chapter to remember the locations.

marking_schemes.question_text: Raghav has been given a project by his teacher in which he has to write about the by-products of an industry that is used for preparing shoe polish, carbon paper and cardboard. Which industry will he be writing about?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Sugar industry
key_points: Sugar industry
marking_schemes.model_answer: Raghav will be writing about the Sugar industry, which produces by-products used for preparing shoe polish, carbon paper, and cardboard.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Mention clearly the difference between products and by-products of certain products in agro-based industries.

marking_schemes.question_text: Raghav has been given a project by his teacher in which he has to write about the by-products of an industry that is used for preparing shoe polish, carbon paper and cardboard. The industry is the Sugar industry. Name any two by-products of the industry mentioned by you.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bagasse. Molasses. Press mud (Any two)
key_points: Any two from: Bagasse, Molasses, Press mud
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two by-products of the sugar industry are Bagasse and Molasses (any two from: Bagasse, Molasses, Press mud).
common_errors: A large number of candidates wrote the products of sugarcane, instead of the 'by-products'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Mention clearly the difference between products and by-products of certain products in agro-based industries.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is a well-developed transport network important for India?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: For industrialisation, urbanisation, tourism, agricultural growth, movement of labour. Integrate the nation/promote employment/education/trade/market/ help in economic development./ Rescue and evacuation during emergency.
key_points: For industrialisation, urbanisation, tourism, agricultural growth, movement of labour
Integrate the nation / promote employment / education / trade / market / help in economic development / rescue and evacuation during emergency
marking_schemes.model_answer: A well-developed transport network is important for India because it facilitates industrialisation, urbanisation, tourism, agricultural growth, and movement of labour. It also helps to integrate the nation, promote trade and employment, and aids in rescue and evacuation during emergencies.
common_errors: A few candidates mentioned only one point of the answer, which made them lose a mark.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give in class repeated explanations on the way to answer questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention any two advantages of road transport.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cheaper, door to door service, flexible, can be made in hilly areas, act as feeder for other means./ Carries Perishable items./ Connect Remote areas Independent/ Available 24 Hours. (any two)
key_points: Any two from: Cheaper, door to door service, flexible, can be made in hilly areas, act as feeder for other means, carries perishable items, connects remote areas, independent, available 24 hours
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two advantages of road transport are that it provides door-to-door service and is flexible, and it can be constructed in hilly areas and connects remote areas that other modes of transport cannot reach.
accepted_alternatives: Can be made in hilly areas
Act as feeder for other means
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss a comparative study of the advantages/disadvantages of different means of transportation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following: The mode of transport that ensures comfortable journey, especially for elders and children.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Railways
key_points: Railways
marking_schemes.model_answer: The mode of transport that ensures comfortable journey, especially for elders and children, is Railways.
common_errors: A few candidates had written Roadways which was an incorrect answer.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to make out the differences between the characteristics of all means of transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following: The highway connecting Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Airways
key_points: East West corridor / expressway / EW corridor
marking_schemes.model_answer: The highway connecting Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat is the East West Corridor (EW Corridor/Expressway).
common_errors: Several candidates gave incorrect answers as the National Highway/North South East West Corridor/Highway.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to read the question carefully before answering.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following: The cheapest means of transport for bulky goods.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Water transport
key_points: Water transport
marking_schemes.model_answer: The cheapest means of transport for bulky goods is Water transport.
common_errors: A few candidates wrote incorrect answers, such as Railways/Roadways.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide a clear description of inland water transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: Airways are the most efficient mode of transport to connect Northeast India with the rest of the country.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Fast, can cross mountains / forest with ease (any one)
key_points: Fast / can cross mountains/forest with ease
marking_schemes.model_answer: Airways are the most efficient mode of transport to connect Northeast India with the rest of the country because they are fast and can cross mountains and forests with ease, overcoming the difficult terrain.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Help students to grasp the importance of airways in modern times.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: Railways are easily developed in the Northern Plains of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Level land, soft soil, agriculturally important, dense population. (any one)
key_points: Level land / soft soil / agriculturally important / dense population
marking_schemes.model_answer: Railways are easily developed in the Northern Plains of India because the land is level and flat, the soil is soft, the area is agriculturally important, and it has a dense population.
common_errors: Majority of the candidates were found to be confused in this question, as they had written incorrectly for the 'Northern Plains', as rugged/roads cannot be constructed and so on.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the various issues related to the railways in detail.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: Rivers of peninsular India are NOT ideal for inland water transport.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Rocky surface, rapids and waterfalls are present, seasonal rivers, uneven topography, rivers are not navigable, short and swift rivers./less deep/presence of hidden rocks. (any one)
key_points: Rocky surface / rapids and waterfalls are present / seasonal rivers / uneven topography / rivers are not navigable / short and swift rivers / less deep / presence of hidden rocks
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rivers of peninsular India are not ideal for inland water transport because they have rocky surfaces, rapids and waterfalls, are seasonal in nature, and are short and swift with uneven topography, making them non-navigable.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Focus more on the types of rivers and their significance for our economic life.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for a substantial rise of E-waste in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Rising use of electronic gadgets./ Modern Lifestyle/ No effective e-waste management system/ Lack of Proper Literacy about e-waste management. (any one)
key_points: Rising use of electronic gadgets / modern lifestyle / no effective e-waste management system / lack of proper literacy about e-waste management
marking_schemes.model_answer: A substantial rise of E-waste in India is due to the rising use of electronic gadgets and modern lifestyle, combined with a lack of an effective e-waste management system.
accepted_alternatives: Lack of Proper Literacy about e-waste management
common_errors: A few candidates incorrectly related it to environmental pollution.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Familiarise students with different types of pollution.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is dumping?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Dumping is a waste disposal method. Waste is collected and taken to large areas on the outskirts of cities where waste is dumped or thrown.
key_points: Dumping is a waste disposal method where waste is collected and taken to large areas on the outskirts of cities where waste is dumped or thrown
marking_schemes.model_answer: Dumping is a waste disposal method in which waste is collected and taken to large areas on the outskirts of cities where it is dumped or thrown.
common_errors: A large number of candidates were confused between the definition of 'dumping' and that of 'landfills' or 'composting'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Describe in detail the important terms in a more elaborate manner.

marking_schemes.question_text: 'You cannot protect environment unless you empower people, you inform them and help them to understand that these resources are their own, that they must protect them.' —Wangari Maathai. As a responsible student how would you contribute to reduce and manage the waste generated in your surroundings. Explain by giving suitable examples.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Waste may be reused such as old clothes, bottles, cans. Cloth bag should be used to reduce use of polythene / less use of plastic.
key_points: Waste may be reused such as old clothes, bottles, cans
Cloth bag should be used to reduce use of polythene / less use of plastic
marking_schemes.model_answer: As a responsible student, I would contribute by reusing waste materials such as old clothes, bottles, and cans, and by using cloth bags to reduce the use of polythene and plastic products.
common_errors: A few candidates mentioned only 3 R's without any explanation.
The remaining few were unable to give proper examples of reducing waste from their day-to-day life.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept of the 3 R's with examples from our daily life.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the 3Rs, give a term that best describes each of the following: An empty soft drink can is used as a pen stand.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Reuse
marking_schemes.model_answer: Reuse
common_errors: A few candidates interchanged answers of iii(a) and iii(b).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept of the 3 R's with examples from our daily life.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the 3Rs, give a term that best describes each of the following: Old scrap papers are used to manufacture handmade paper.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Recycle
marking_schemes.model_answer: Recycle
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept of the 3 R's with examples from our daily life.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the 3Rs, give a term that best describes each of the following: No food is wasted in the household.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Reduce
marking_schemes.model_answer: Reduce
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept of the 3 R's with examples from our daily life.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following statement: Organic manure should replace chemical fertilisers.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is eco-friendly / does not harm the soil or environment / good for growing healthy crops./checks soil pollution./Retain soil moisture./ Checks Biomagnification./ Eutrophication./ Supress Plant Diseases. (any one)
key_points: Eco-friendly / does not harm the soil or environment / good for growing healthy crops / checks soil pollution / retains soil moisture / checks Biomagnification / Eutrophication / suppresses plant diseases
marking_schemes.model_answer: Organic manure should replace chemical fertilisers because it is eco-friendly, does not harm the soil or environment, helps in growing healthy crops, and checks soil pollution and Biomagnification.
accepted_alternatives: Does not harm the soil or environment
common_errors: Several candidates did not understand the question properly.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in class the importance of organic fertilizers over chemical fertilizers.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following statement: There should be a ban on the use of polythene and plastic products.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It leads to pollution / takes long time to decompose./harmful/non-biodegradable (any one)
key_points: Leads to pollution / takes long time to decompose / harmful / non-biodegradable
marking_schemes.model_answer: There should be a ban on the use of polythene and plastic products because they lead to pollution, take a very long time to decompose, and are non-biodegradable and harmful to the environment.
common_errors: Majority of the candidates made errors in this part of the question, as they found the language and understanding of the concept difficult.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept of Biomagnification and Eutrophication.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following statement: Manual handling of waste must be avoided.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It leads to health hazards.
key_points: It leads to health hazards
marking_schemes.model_answer: Manual handling of waste must be avoided because it leads to health hazards for the workers involved.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss elaborately in class the health hazards related to manual handling of the waste.
